definition: A stated rule of thumb for a two-breakdown transition (one breakdown biased toward the starting pose, one biased toward the ending pose): by default, use a SIMILAR percentage bias on both breakdowns (e.g. both biased 70% toward their nearer pose) rather than choosing each independently, reserving deliberately mismatched bias for when an asymmetric ease-in/ease-out is specifically wanted.
purpose: Give a sensible, low-effort default for the common case (a roughly symmetric ease-out/ease-in feel) while leaving the door open to deliberately break symmetry when a transition should accelerate differently than it decelerates.
visible_effect: The fastest point of the motion sits at the midpoint between the two breakdowns; a symmetric bias choice puts that fastest point at the geometric middle of the whole transition, while an asymmetric one shifts it toward whichever end has the smaller bias.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: A symmetric default feels balanced and matches the shape of ordinary slow-in/slow-out; a deliberately asymmetric choice (a fast whip-out followed by a slow, lingering arrival, or vice versa) reads as a specific stylistic choice rather than an accident, precisely because it departs from the default.
physical_interpretation: not applicable — a stated authoring default/heuristic, not a physical claim.
use_cases: a first pass on any two-breakdown transition, where matching the bias percentage on both ends is a reasonable starting point before any deliberate asymmetry is considered
non_use_cases: a transition that should read as, for example, an explosive start with a long lingering settle (or the reverse) — there, mismatched bias is the correct choice from the start, not a default to override later
interactions: progressive_spacing_via_pose_density_before_curve_interpolation (this same batch, video 94) — this entry is a specific numeric convention used WITHIN that broader workflow, not a separate principle.
cadence_representation: Not represented: `ai/plan.js`'s breakdown step requires an explicit numeric `bias` per call with no default value and no linkage between two breakdowns of the same transition — Cadence enforces THAT a bias must be stated (see progressive_spacing_via_pose_density_before_curve_interpolation, this same batch) but has no notion of keeping two breakdowns' bias values symmetric by convention; that judgment call is entirely on the caller today.
control_surface: `authorMotion`'s breakdown step's `bias` parameter, called twice per transition with no built-in relationship enforced between the two calls.
detection_and_measurement_methods: not measurable in this build — a caller-side default/convention, not a property of a resulting track.
generation_or_modification_methods: not applicable — no Cadence operation currently applies or suggests a default bias value.
failure_modes: choosing wildly different bias values for the two breakdowns of one transition without a specific stylistic reason, producing an unintentionally lopsided ease that reads as a mistake rather than a choice
examples: the presenter's own words, verbatim: 'I almost always use a similar percentage bias on my breakdown 2 towards pose B that I used on my breakdown one towards pose a[.] it's a general rule of thumb' (transcript 5:56-6:04)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/v71G6TCw_0M @ 5:46-6:04 — Chester Sampson states the symmetric-bias-by-default rule of thumb directly, transcript-only per this video's detail setting; experimental until validated
